memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The Lord will establish you as his holy people, as he promised you on oath, if you keep the commands of the Lord your God and walk in obedience to him. Then all the peoples on earth will see that you are called by the name of the Lord, and they will fear you." — Deut 28:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Beyond crops and victories, God promised Israel something far greater: to establish them as "his holy people." This was the heart of the blessing. To be marked out as God's own, called by His name, distinct among all the nations — that was the true treasure. And the watching world would notice that this people belonged to the Lord.

To be "called by the name of the Lord" is a stunning privilege. It means belonging to God, bearing His reputation, being identified with Him before a watching world. Israel's calling was not merely to be prosperous, but to be holy — set apart to reflect the character of the God they served.

If you are in Christ, this identity is yours in an even deeper way. Peter takes this very language and applies it to the church: you are "a holy nation, God's special possession," called out of darkness to declare His praises (1 Pet 2:9). You bear the name of your God before a watching world.

That is both a comfort and a calling. A comfort, because you belong to Him. A calling, because the world sees God through people who bear His name. So live in a way that honours the One whose name you carry. Let your life quietly show the world that you belong to the Lord.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I live aware that I bear the name of the Lord before a watching world?
2. Am I seeking holiness, or only comfort and blessing?
3. What might others learn about God by watching my life this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for calling me by Your name and setting me apart as Your own. Help me live a holy life that honours You before the watching world. Amen.
